sources.entry: Crisp - Free AI photo upscaler that runs entirely in your browser. No upload, no signup, no watermark. Includes a dedicated anime upscaler. #free

summary.name: Crisp
summary.one_liner: Crisp (crisp.photos) is a free browser-based AI image upscaler that enlarges JPG, PNG and WebP photos 4× without uploading them to a server.
use_cases: enlarge a small photo to 4x its size
sharpen or unblur a blurry photo
upscale a photo to 4K or 8K resolution
create a before/after comparison video of an upscaled photo
upscale images privately without uploading them
summary.what_it_does: Crisp upscales images 4× directly in the browser using the 4x-UltraSharpV2_Lite super-resolution model by Kim2091, optimised for WebGPU. Images are said to stay on the user's device rather than being uploaded. Supported inputs are JPG, PNG and WebP, and the result downloads as PNG. The page says the tool can recover fine detail to sharpen blurry or low-resolution photos. After upscaling, users can export a sliding before/after MP4 video, and a separate free Before/After Video Generator tool is linked for comparing any two images. The page also mentions a dedicated anime upscaler via the directory listing.
notable: Runs entirely in the browser; images stated to never leave the device
No sign-up, no watermarks, no limits per the page
Exports sliding before/after MP4 comparison video
Uses 4x-UltraSharpV2_Lite model, faster with WebGPU and a GPU
caveats: Model weights are licensed CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, which restricts commercial use
Anonymous usage statistics are logged, per the page
Performance depends on browser and GPU; WebGPU makes it much faster
